payload.name: decimation
payload.scope: Human-made signal processing technique for reducing the sample rate of a digital signal by an integer factor through anti-aliasing filtering and downsampling.

payload.body: Decimation is a human-made signal processing technique that reduces the sample rate of a discrete signal by an integer factor M. Parameters: decimation factor M (>1), anti-aliasing low-pass filter (cutoff ≤ new Nyquist frequency), and the downsampling operation (keep every Mth sample). The two-step mechanism: (1) anti-aliasing filter removes frequencies that would alias at the reduced rate, (2) downsampling discards samples to achieve the lower rate. Persistence mechanism: implemented in DSP software libraries, audio toolchains, and hardware DSP chips; documented in standard signal processing textbooks. [formal: decimation | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

payload.name: pre-ringing
payload.scope: Human-made signal processing phenomenon: transient overshoot before a step change in a filtered signal, caused by linear-phase filter design.

payload.body: Pre-ringing is a human-made signal processing artifact where a filtered signal exhibits transient overshoot or oscillation before a sudden step change or impulse. Parameters: filter type (linear-phase FIR, linear-phase IIR), filter order, cutoff frequency, and the signal's step edge characteristics. Mechanism: symmetric impulse response of linear-phase filters spreads filter energy equally before and after the impulse, causing perceptible pre-ringing on sharp transients. Persistence mechanism: inherent property of linear-phase filter implementations; documented in DSP literature; perceptually significant in audio processing where pre-ringing is more objectionable than post-ringing. [formal: pre-ringing | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.03]
